news.title: FIFA's World Cup sale plan met with shock and anger
news.lede: A proposal that could reshape the commercial future of the World Cup has sparked fierce opposition from football's governing bodies. FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday unveiled plans to create a $20 billion (€17.5 billion) company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to run competitions including the World Cup and Club World Cup with private investors, according to The Times of London. Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter voiced concern over the close ties between Infantino and US President Donald Trump, as Thrive Eternal, led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, is among the reported potential investors. Meanwhile, EU Commissioner for Sport Glenn Micallef wrote on X: "Hands off our game."

news.title: Uefa calls emergency meeting as opposition to Fifa plan hardens
news.lede: 55 members to meet on Thursday to coordinate response. ‘Uefa knows there is significant and growing opposition’. Uefa has called an emergency meeting of their 55 members for Thursday afternoon to discuss a coordinated response to Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, with a European boycott of Fifa tournaments among the options under consideration. The Guardian has been told that, as the next major event in the Fifa calendar, a boycott of next year’s Women’s World Cup has been mentioned in preliminary discussions, although there would be a reluctance in some quarters to make the women’s game suffer as a result as consequence of a protest against Fifa proposals that primarily revolve around monetising the men’s World Cup and Club World Cup.

news.title: ‘It is not FIFA’s to sell’ - Gianni Infantino’s $20 billion World Cup power play puts soccer’s soul up for sale - and makes resistance too expensive
news.lede: Gianni Infantino’s move to sell stakes in FIFA’s commercial rights is part of a disheartening trend stripping the soul from professional sports. Earlier this week, Gianni Infantino got a little bit angry. In a 15-slide Instagram post, the FIFA President took on all of the criticism of the 2026 World Cup. It was, effectively, a laundry list of his accomplishments, accompanied, pointedly, by counterarguments to every single pre-tournament grievance.

news.title: World Cup: FIFA chief Gianni Infantino offers £30m incentive for members to back controversial private investment plans
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has given football associations until September 19 to back his plan to sell off part of FIFA to private investors with a £30.1m ($40m) incentive to accept, a letter has revealed. FIFA announced on Tuesday that it was seeking to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would bring together the sale of FIFA's commercial rights - including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing - with the operational delivery of its tournaments. Under the proposal, FIFA would raise up to £3.1bn ($4.2bn) from external investors by selling minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it says would be valued at around £15bn ($20bn). The governing body says its plans - which need approval from member associations - could deliver more than £7.53bn ($10bn) in "football development funding" over the next four years.

news.title: Dutch FA speaks out against FIFA's plan to sell off World Cup
news.lede: The Dutch Football (KNVB) has become the latest major governing body to voice its opposition to FIFA president Gianni Infantino's controversial proposal to sell off stakes in the World Cup. The plan, which involves private investors taking ownership in a new commercial subsidiary, has sparked a civil war within the global game. The KNVB has joined a growing chorus of disapproval from European football's heavyweights regarding FIFA's attempt to privatise its most prestigious assets. Under the drafted proposal, a new $20 billion subsidiary would be established to manage the commercial rights of the World Cup and the renovated Club World Cup, with 20 per cent of the company being offloaded to private equity firms.

news.title: The Guardian view on selling off the World Cup: a red-card offence by Gianni Infantino | Editorial
news.lede: Fifa’s president hopes to sell stakes in the planet’s most watched sporting event. In the wider interests of football, he must be resisted. Like a sporting Dr Pangloss, Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, would like to persuade football followers that they are living in the best of all possible worlds. Maddeningly for him, many disagree.

news.title: Where To Find Egypt's Stars After Their 2026 World Cup Elimination
news.lede: Egypt earned a place in the knockout rounds of the 2026 World Cup. The team advanced past the group stage to compete in the elimination rounds of the tournament. During the group stage, they defeated New Zealand and drew against Belgium and Iran. Mohamed Salah contributed an assist in the opening match against Belgium and recorded both a goal and an assist against New Zealand to help secure Egypt's progression.
